sourceBindings.text: Prepare two different case records
Observation and affected leaf age/location
At least two competing explanations
Soil/root/weather evidence and uncertainty
Test or observation that could change the hypothesis
Water priority, conditional method and scheduling evidence
Right source and why it is appropriate
Right rate: evidence or missing data, not a made-up number
Right time and loss-risk condition
Right place, product/seed safety and feasibility
Potential loss pathway, costs and alternative
Individual explanation and exit record
Which one case will you defend and why?
What criticism or new evidence would change your recommendation?
Exit: K leaf-margin clue and a reasoned method for very sandy soil
Text presence opens comparison only; it does not validate causal reasoning.

These online tasks rehearse reasoning only. Typed completeness and correct choices do not establish a diagnosis, a real field treatment or criterion mastery; the case explanations need trainer review.

units.delivery: Explain calmly and naturally to agricultural vocational learners in clear English. Read only the supplied connected passage with natural pauses. Preserve all negations, conditions, scene-safety restrictions and limits of training. Do not add medical advice, diagnoses, character voices, an introduction, music or an extra summary.

sourceBindings.text: For tomato, wheat, leafy planning and cold maize, labels facts separately from hypotheses, gives plausible alternatives, identifies a next observation/test, and places correction of actual standing-water/root stress before fertilizer advice.
Pass only with evidence and competing explanations; naming a deficiency from one leaf image or afternoon wilt alone needs guided retry.

For each proposed nutrient action identifies source, rate evidence, timing and placement; rate requires soil/crop data and suitable local guidance. Describes calcium nitrate as N plus Ca, not NPK; avoids automatic urea, DAP or foliar K from symptoms.
Pass when all four R's and water priority fit the scenario and do not include an unsupported dose or calendar.

Submits two complete case sheets, gives one defended presentation or equivalent oral/written explanation and critiques alternatives for the remaining cases. For the 45-minute trainer workshop, contribution and reasoning are captured individually even if groups discuss together.
Pass on two complete, evidence-based cases plus one defended explanation; participation or a group answer alone does not establish the individual's reasoning.

The trainer may facilitate a 45-minute case discussion using prepared cards and observe reasoning. This is not a signed field-diagnosis or fertilizer-application skill. Any real field advice requires local testing and qualified supervision.
Which symptom did you initially overinterpret, what test would change your mind, and which of the four R decisions still lacks evidence?
No observation, trainer decision or signature has been recorded. Complete them only after actual supervised work.
